command:
set +e
set -uo pipefail
export PATH=/opt/conda/bin:$PATH
export TMPDIR=/tmp HOME=/tmp
cd /tmp
# Pre-create the declared logs so a run that dies still stages its evidence.
: > construct.log; : > paths.log; : > view.log

# spawn runs task commands under bash -e; `set -uo pipefail` does not clear it (spawn#707).
# PATH export IS needed: aarchbio images have their PATH dropped by the task shell.
#
# NOTHING NEW IS STAGED. chr20.fa comes from the bwa fixture and the VCF is the GIAB chr20
# truth set already staged for gatk4 -- so the graph is built from bytes other recipes in this
# catalog have already verified.

echo "== the inputs must be the bytes the linear-reference recipes use =="
REFBASES=$(tail -n +2 chr20.fa | tr -d '\n' | wc -c | tr -d ' ')
printf 'reference_bases\t%s\n' "$REFBASES"
test "$REFBASES" = "64444167" || { echo "FAIL: chr20.fa has $REFBASES bases, the staged fixture has 64444167"; exit 1; }
NVAR=$(zcat truth.chr20.vcf.gz | grep -vc '^#')
printf 'input_variants\t%s\n' "$NVAR"
test "$NVAR" -gt 50000 || { echo "FAIL: only $NVAR variants"; exit 1; }

vg version 2>&1 | head -2

echo "== build the graph: linear reference plus 82,818 real variants =="
T0=$(date +%s)
vg construct -r chr20.fa -v truth.chr20.vcf.gz -R chr20 -t "$(nproc)" > chr20.vg 2> construct.log
RC=$?
T1=$(date +%s)
printf 'construct_rc\t%s\n' "$RC"
printf 'construct_wall_s\t%s\n' "$((T1-T0))"
test "$RC" = "0" || { tail -25 construct.log; echo "FAIL: vg construct exited $RC"; exit 1; }
test -s chr20.vg || { echo "FAIL: vg construct wrote no graph"; exit 1; }
ls -l chr20.vg | awk '{print "graph_bytes\t"$5}'

echo "== graph structure =="
vg stats -z -l chr20.vg > stats.txt 2>&1
cat stats.txt | sed 's/^/  /'
NODES=$(awk '$1=="nodes"{print $2}' stats.txt)
EDGES=$(awk '$1=="edges"{print $2}' stats.txt)
GLEN=$(awk '$1=="length"{print $2}' stats.txt)
printf 'nodes\t%s\n' "$NODES"
printf 'edges\t%s\n' "$EDGES"
printf 'graph_total_length\t%s\n' "$GLEN"
test -n "$NODES" -a -n "$GLEN" || { echo "FAIL: could not read vg stats"; exit 1; }

# ------------------------------------------- THE IDENTITY: the graph still contains the genome
# A variation graph embeds the reference as a named path. Walking that path must reproduce the
# input FASTA CHARACTER FOR CHARACTER -- the graph is a lossless re-encoding of the linear
# reference plus alternatives, so anything else means construction corrupted or dropped
# sequence. This is exact: a sha256 over the sequence, no tolerance.
echo "== extract the reference path and compare it to the input, byte for byte =="
vg paths -F -x chr20.vg > paths.fa 2> paths.log
PRC=$?
printf 'paths_rc\t%s\n' "$PRC"
test "$PRC" = "0" || { tail -20 paths.log; echo "FAIL: vg paths exited $PRC"; exit 1; }
grep '^>' paths.fa | head -5 | sed 's/^/  path: /'
NPATH=$(grep -c '^>' paths.fa)
printf 'paths_in_graph\t%s\n' "$NPATH"

# Normalise both sides identically: drop headers, drop newlines, uppercase. That removes FASTA
# line-wrapping and case conventions, which are formatting rather than sequence -- what is
# being compared is the base string itself.
tail -n +2 chr20.fa | tr -d '\n' | tr 'acgtn' 'ACGTN' > ref.seq
awk '/^>/{next} {printf "%s", $0}' paths.fa | tr 'acgtn' 'ACGTN' > path.seq
REFLEN=$(wc -c < ref.seq | tr -d ' ')
PATHLEN=$(wc -c < path.seq | tr -d ' ')
REFSHA=$(sha256sum ref.seq | awk '{print $1}')
PATHSHA=$(sha256sum path.seq | awk '{print $1}')
printf 'ref_seq_length\t%s\n' "$REFLEN"
printf 'path_seq_length\t%s\n' "$PATHLEN"
printf 'ref_seq_sha256\t%s\n' "$REFSHA"
printf 'path_seq_sha256\t%s\n' "$PATHSHA"

test "$PATHLEN" = "$REFLEN" || {
  echo "FAIL: the reference path is $PATHLEN bases, the input is $REFLEN"; exit 1; }
test "$PATHSHA" = "$REFSHA" || {
  echo "FAIL: the reference path does not spell the input back -- sha256 differs"
  cmp ref.seq path.seq 2>&1 | head -3
  exit 1; }
printf 'identity_refpath\tthe graph reference path spells chr20.fa back exactly (%s)\n' "$REFSHA"

# ------------------------------------------- arithmetic: the graph is bigger by the alt bases
# Total graph sequence = reference length + novel sequence contributed by alternate alleles.
# Reported rather than asserted: the exact novel-base count depends on how vg merges identical
# alt sequence between overlapping variants, which is an implementation choice, not arithmetic
# this recipe can predict.
awk -v g="$GLEN" -v r="$REFLEN" 'BEGIN{printf "graph_minus_reference\t%d\talt sequence added\n", g-r}'

# odgi reads GFA, not vg's native serialisation, so the graph is exported in the interchange
# format the next task actually consumes. GFA is also what makes the cross-check meaningful:
# both tools parse the same text, so any disagreement is about interpretation rather than
# about one of them reading a format the other wrote.
echo "== export GFA for the odgi cross-check =="
vg view -g chr20.vg > chr20.gfa 2> view.log
VRC=$?
printf 'gfa_rc\t%s\n' "$VRC"
test "$VRC" = "0" || { tail -20 view.log; echo "FAIL: vg view exited $VRC"; exit 1; }
test -s chr20.gfa || { echo "FAIL: vg view wrote no GFA"; exit 1; }
ls -l chr20.gfa | awk '{print "gfa_bytes\t"$5}'
GFASEG=$(awk '$1=="S"' chr20.gfa | wc -l | tr -d ' ')
printf 'gfa_segments\t%s\n' "$GFASEG"
test "$GFASEG" = "$NODES" || { echo "FAIL: GFA has $GFASEG segments, vg stats said $NODES nodes"; exit 1; }
printf 'identity_gfa\tGFA segment count matches vg node count (%s)\n' "$GFASEG"

{ printf 'observable\tvalue\n'
  printf 'reference_bases\t%s\n' "$REFBASES"
  printf 'input_variants\t%s\n' "$NVAR"
  printf 'nodes\t%s\nedges\t%s\ngraph_total_length\t%s\n' "$NODES" "$EDGES" "$GLEN"
  printf 'paths_in_graph\t%s\n' "$NPATH"
  printf 'ref_seq_sha256\t%s\n' "$REFSHA"
  printf 'path_seq_sha256\t%s\n' "$PATHSHA"; } > vg_score.tsv
printf 'nodes\t%s\nedges\t%s\ngraph_total_length\t%s\n' "$NODES" "$EDGES" "$GLEN" > vg_structure.tsv
rm -f ref.seq path.seq paths.fa
echo "VG OK"
